title: Opportunity
paragraphs: "In terms of technology and logistics, no one can match Faubrey and Zeltoble. But if we're talking about the combat strength of individual citizens, it's got to be Siltvelt, right? Until recently, Shieldfreeden was known for being relatively peaceful, with advanced technology and high combat capabilities... I guess its strength lies in being a powerful nation overall."
“By the way, what about Melromarc?”

“Huh? Well, I guess it’s a reasonably strong country? It’s not the kind of place demi-humans and Therianthropes would be eager to go to, so I’m just going by what I’ve heard, though. I’ve heard that in the wars of the past, it was strong enough to deal a major blow to every country—enough to effectively defeat Siltvelt, even.”
In terms of national power, Faubrey and Zeltoble are the top two, followed by Siltvelt, Shieldfreeden, and Melromarc, I suppose.

“They say the queen of Melromarc—known as the ‘She-Fox’—has formed an alliance with a wise and wise king, and she’s skilled at resolving or deflecting various issues through diplomacy. I’ve even heard that it was thanks to her that the spark of war Zeltoble was trying to ignite was extinguished.”
“Wow, so the queen is that capable?”
“They say she’s a smooth talker. We’ll probably end up meeting her someday, so you’d better be careful, okay?”
“She’s certainly capable. But given her personality, I don’t think we’ll be at odds with her.”

At least in every loop so far, the queen has never become an enemy. That’s probably because the Queen views the ‘Wave’ as a threat. So if the ‘Wave’ didn’t exist, the situation might have been different.
“I don’t know about that… It just looks like she played her cards right again this time, too.”
Panda seems to be suspicious of the Queen. As far as I’m concerned, the Queen is a convenient ally, but I suppose that’s how she comes across to a mercenary.
“Well… speaking of Shieldfreeden, how does it look to you, Larsa?”
“Honestly, I think the disparity among the citizens is pretty extreme.”
“Ah… yeah, you’re right.”

I’ll take a look outside in place of Father. That’s certainly true. There isn’t much of a disparity between Demi-Humans, Therianthropes, and humans, but I see a lot of people whose clothes look worn out. On the other hand, there are also those wearing what look like expensive clothes. It doesn’t seem like the groups are mixing. Just as I was thinking that, a welcoming procession consisting entirely of Demi-Humans appeared.
“We’ve entered Demi-Human District.”
“Demi-Human District?”
“That’s right. In Shieldfreeden, there are separate districts—one where only Demi-Humans can enter, and another where only humans can enter.”
“Even though it’s a country where Demi-Humans and humans are equal?”

“I don’t really know much about it either. But there are times when people just can’t relax unless they’re with their own kind. I hear they’ve divided the city into these districts to alleviate that kind of stress.”
“Was there a place like that in Faubrey?”
“There’s a residential district reserved exclusively for the royal family. I don’t know about the general populace, though.”

Isn’t it a residential district reserved exclusively for the royal family, like the one in Faubrey? I seem to vaguely remember it. I’m pretty sure that was in the first world. I’ve been there in the world after peace was established. We didn’t stop by during Filo-chan’s IN Live Tour, though.
“What’s that?”
“There are towns where you can’t live unless you have royal blood in your veins. Though, as far as race goes, they seemed to be a real mixed bag.”
“That’s because the lineage there comes from the Hero. If you have the Hero’s blood, they don’t care about race. Everyone else gets along just fine.”
“As for Zeltoble… there’s no such district there.”
“Over there, money is everything. If you want to hang out with your own kind, why not just go to a specialty shop?”
“Huh… there sure are all kinds of places.”
“Everyone has different views. If you start worrying about it, there’s no end to it.”
“It’s a country that’s kind of hard to wrap my head around… especially Shieldfreeden.”
“Well, all their representatives throughout history have been from the country of Demi-Humans, after all.”

In other words, even though they tout themselves as a land of freedom, there’s still a hierarchy based on race. I’m no Panda, but if you start worrying about it, there’s no end to it. To be honest, I couldn’t care less.
“Ah, I see.”

With Father letting out a sigh like that, the carriage continued on its way. Along the road, the people of Shieldfreeden—suppressing their anxiety—were waving flags as if to welcome the Shield Hero’s visit. And so, we arrived at the building where the representatives of Shieldfreeden were gathered.

In Shieldfreeden, the representatives’ residence appears to be a strange building—one that’s hard to even call a castle, given its massive width. We made our way inside that building. Oh, of course, we were on high alert in case terrorists might try something, but thanks to either prior reconnaissance or the thorough checks conducted by the people of Siltvelt, it seems the situation has been securely resolved.
“W-well now… Thank you so much for coming to our Shieldfreeden. Shield Hero, Spear Hero.”
A group of people who appeared to be Shieldfreeden’s representatives—their faces pale and trembling slightly—welcomed Father and me while being watched over by the people from Siltvelt.

“This war was caused by Nelshen, the representative of the Aotatsu race who served as the nation’s representative, who privately abused Shieldfreeden’s full authority based on false information. I’m sure you Heroes can understand that this does not reflect the collective will of the people of Shieldfreeden.”
HAHAHA. What a way to start off. Do you really think that joke will fly with Father? He narrows his eyes—as if he’s switched into “merchant mode”—and glares at the representatives.
“So what you’re saying is… even though you caused all this commotion, the former representative took full responsibility for it, so you guys aren’t at fault at all?”
“N-no… that’s not exactly what I meant…”

“You could have spoken up and said that war is wrong, couldn’t you? Yet, to satisfy your own sense of justice, you went along with the former representative’s selfish revenge—and now you think you can just flip-flop and claim you were deceived if you lose?”
As the representatives stammer and mumble their way through their response, Father launches another attack.
“I want you to think about this: when Siltvelt loses and the truth comes out, do you think you’d have grilled the former representative’s Takt faction the same way?”
“W-well… we could!”
HAHAHA, that’s impossible. Even if you could, you’d just get wiped out by the Takt faction and that’d be the end of it.

“Anyone can say that when the other side isn’t even here anymore. So why not actually take action? You’re the ones who didn’t, right? We’ve been constantly reporting on the events that occurred in diplomacy, so you’ve already given your answer.”

Father’s rhetorical tactic of letting them run with it before cutting them off is really on full display here. The people from Shieldfreeden are apologizing, but you can tell by the look in their eyes that they’re not truly sorry.
“They’re probably thinking, ‘For a young upstart from another world, you sure act all high and mighty…’”
When Father muttered that under his breath, some of the Shieldfreeden members looked away. I suppose he’d hit the nail on the head.

“Even so, I’ve come here as the Shield Hero, bearing the weight of Siltvelt on my shoulders. I’ve come to inspect the uncooperative Shieldfreeden in order to protect the world from the threat of the waves. You understand that, don’t you?”
“Y-yes! We’re fully aware of that!”
“For someone who claims that, it seems there were some factions that gave me a rather rough welcome. Is your security as full of holes as a sieve?”
How is that any different from a simple ring, I wonder?
“The former representative’s rampage… For someone who’s supposed to be as resilient as a lizard’s tail, I think their follow-up actions have been rather half-hearted.”

Seizing the moment, Father is rubbing it in to the people of Shieldfreeden with all the sarcasm he can muster. The other side just keeps turning pale and seems unable to do anything but bow their heads.
“If you keep pulling these kinds of stunts… you’d better consider the possibility that the nation of Shieldfreeden might cease to exist.”
“Eek!?”
Father’s menacing voice, my murderous intent, and the people from Siltvelt are all heaping threats upon the Shieldfreeden delegation without holding back.
“How do you think the world will view such behavior—”

“Shieldfreeden’s noble cause is already a thing of the past, isn’t it? Even the great nation of Faubrey has left the matter entirely in Siltvelt’s hands. This is a country that cooperated with Takt, who tarnished the Legend of the Hero. Public opinion is already calling for you and your nation to vanish… Surely your leadership isn’t so corrupt as to be unaware of that, is it?”

I’m sure they don’t get it. How should I put it? They seem like the kind of people who can’t even imagine the worst-case scenario—what kind of punishment they’ll face if they make the wrong choice. It’s clear they still think of themselves as a major power.
“Numbers are powerless against a Hero, you know? You should have learned that firsthand in the last battle.”
I’ll go along with Father’s threats, too. As long as this Motoyasu Ai remains in the shadows, I won’t tolerate any of your reckless actions.
“Aaaaaah…”
The people of Shieldfreeden seem to be so terrified by our threats that they’ve lost all their nerve. Hahaha, how pathetic.
“I came here to give a chance to Shieldfreeden, and this is how it ends…”
“Please! Please, give us a chance!”
The people of Shieldfreeden bowed deeply to Father, as if begging for mercy. Hmm… Their reaction looks familiar. It’s just like I used to be. I can’t help but feel a twinge of sympathy.
Hmm… It seems Father wanted to steer things in this direction after all. Well then, I suppose I’ll go along with his plan.
“Father, how about giving them a chance?”
Father looked at me with a puzzled expression at my suggestion. Then he turned his gaze back to the people from Shieldfreeden and crossed his arms.
“…And so, Motoyasu—the Spear Hero—has granted us a reprieve. To ensure this never happens again, focus your efforts not only on security but also on cracking down on those who resist!”
“H-ha ha!”
After saying that, some of the Shieldfreeden members left the room to relay the orders.

“...Well then, regarding the issues ahead, let’s hold a meeting with the representatives of this country. That’s what I’d like to do, but the journey here has left us all a bit tired. I’d like to take a short break—is that okay?”
“Yes!”

The Shieldfreeden members nodded, and at the suggestion of the Siltvelt members, we were escorted to a fairly large room within the facility. Of course, we’d already checked for any underhanded traps set by the enemy, so there’s no problem there. The panda therianthropes seem to be standing by at the entrance, ready to deal with any intruders at any time. Yuki-chan and the others went to the back of the room and started sitting down in chairs.
“Phew… Seriously, these people make me want to ask if they even realize they’re representing their country.”
“Isn’t that just how the upper echelons of a country are supposed to be?”
“The royalty I’ve known were much more motivated and had a stronger sense of responsibility, though.”

At the very least, I think the Queen of Melromarc and her Finacée are excellent representatives. As for Trash… well, that’s a bit of a mixed bag. Setting aside what happened after his awakening, in most loops he was the very picture of incompetence. Well, according to Father, politics is prone to corruption, so maybe it can’t be helped.
“I’d really like to leave it to someone that capable…”
“Then shall we leave it entirely up to the Queen of Melromarc?”
“What are you talking about?”
Panda nearly tripped at my suggestion, then shot me a look of utter exasperation. What’s the matter? Are you saying my opinion is crazy?
“Listen, Motoyasu. Melromarc is an enemy nation when it comes to countries dealing with Demi-Humans, right? There’s no way we can entrust Melromarc with the provisional governance of Shieldfreeden.”

But in my original world, Trash and his Finacée meddled in Shieldfreeden’s politics in all sorts of ways and silenced everyone. They also fleeced the country handsomely through postwar reparations and the like, which sparked quite a bit of internal strife—and I seem to recall that, in the ensuing chaos, the country was actually governed quite effectively… I think. Though, mind you, this is just secondhand information.
“In the world you know, Motoyasu-kun, you might have been able to pull off all sorts of reckless stunts, but in this world, we can’t pull off reforms that bold.”
“Hmm… Politics really is a tricky business, isn’t it?”
Well, I suppose that means it’s too much of a burden to leave entirely up to Melromarc right now.
“I went to Siltvelt in the first place because I wanted to teach Melromarc a lesson, didn’t I? What’s the point of letting them have it easy?”
Ah, that’s right. Thanks to Éclair, we managed to minimize the damage, but originally, our goal was to take down the Trash from Melromarc and the Three Heroes Church.

“Even with Motoyasu-kun’s knowledge, the only outstanding leaders who leave a strong impression seem to be from Melromarc and that sort of place. Once we’ve done some research, wouldn’t it make sense to leave it to someone trustworthy in Siltvelt…?”
“I suppose that’s the sensible thing to do, isn’t it? Though I’m not really in a position to have a say on that, mind you.”
“It’d be a big help if you could share what you know. I still don’t know much about this world yet.”
That’s the kind of conversation Father was having with Panda.
“So, there’s something that’s been on my mind.”
“What is it?”
“I know this might be a bit rude, but is there some ulterior motive behind Motoyasu-kun offering the people of Shieldfreeden this opportunity?”

“An ulterior motive, you say? It seems Father is reading too much into this, thinking I had some hidden agenda when I gave the people of Shieldfreeden that opportunity. But there really isn’t any deep reason behind it.
“…You see, after countless failures, I, too, was once given one last chance.”
